title: Om as Its Measures
meter: Prose (the Upanishad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Mandukya Upanishad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pada and matra, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
translation: This Self, seen as a syllable, is Om; seen as measures: the quarters are the measures and the measures are the quarters, namely A, U and M.
translation_hi: यह आत्मा अक्षर की दृष्टि से ओंकार है, और मात्राओं की दृष्टि से: पाद ही मात्राएँ हैं और मात्राएँ ही पाद हैं, अर्थात् अकार, उकार और मकार।

words.note: Also: the matras (morae) the meter scanner counts!

grammar: Pada and matra: the Upanishad maps the four quarters of the Self onto the measures of Om, using the exact words Sanskrit prosody uses for a verse's quarters and its syllable lengths.
-kara 'sound': अकार, उकार, मकार; Om itself is ओङ्कार, 'the Om-sound'.
Om = A + U + M: in sandhi, अ + उ → ओ (guna), then म्: अ-उ-म् → ओम्.
